input:
Once the corrosion allowance has been added in, the wall thickness of the absorber comes to 35 mm, and the shell as specified is able to meet the design duty at that thickness without any further step up in plate being required. It is worth being clear that this figure is the finished thickness, with the allowance already included; the pressure-resisting part of the wall is what is left once the allowance has been taken off, and the plate itself is ordered to the finished figure.

Turning to the flanged joints on the absorber, the two gasket materials under consideration are compared on the basis of temperature limit only. The lower-rated material would serve perfectly well at the normal operating temperature of the joint, and on that ground alone it might well be chosen, for ease of seating and for cost. The higher-rated material is nevertheless preferred. The reason is that the joint at the discharge of the lean solvent pump sees the highest temperature anywhere on the unit during a loss of cooling, and a gasket that has been chosen for the normal temperature alone has in effect been chosen for the milder of the two duties that the joint is required to meet; the rating of the higher-rated material covers both of those duties, and the temperature limit, which is the stated ground of the comparison, is the property that decides the matter during
